**P. aeruginosa** produces the largest |ΔCD| with BA@L-HGNRs in Fig. 2a (page 5).

- Its bar is the tallest, at roughly 190 mdeg. This is read from the graph; the text does not give an exact number.
- The bars decrease in this order: P. aeruginosa > E. coli > E. sakazakii > S. typhimurium > E. faecium > L. monocytogenes > S. aureus. S. aureus is the smallest, at roughly 10–15 mdeg.
- The BA@D-HGNRs bars are nearly the same height for each bacterium. The paper uses this to argue that the response is "largely independent" of the probe's stereochemical configuration (page 5).

The same ranking appears in the ΔCD bar chart in Fig. 2d (page 5). It also fits the paper's choice of P. aeruginosa as the model bacterium for optimizing the NaCl conditions (page 4).
